schema_review.rationale: Revisions v1_5_0_006 and v1_5_0_007 follow v1_5_0_005 on both registered source chains and all vector/Code profiles. v1_5_0_006 adds one NOT NULL column with a server default, pc_scopes.lifecycle_state over ('writable','archived','deleting','deleted'), so every existing Scope reads back 'writable' without a data rewrite or a retroactive state change. v1_5_0_007 adds two new tables, pc_scope_deletions and pc_scope_deletion_progress, which hold one explicit deletion's operation identity, the exact confirmed structural set and versions, and one progress row per member and owned-resource handler; the progress table's only foreign key is to its own operation. Access cutoff stays in pc_scopes.lifecycle_state, so deletion adds no column to any existing table. Neither revision alters an existing table, index, foreign key, check constraint or row, and Artifact, Source, Candidate, processing, publication and evidence storage keep their exact shape, so v1_5_0_005 and v1_5_0_006 keep their recorded schema fingerprints and an upgraded database retains every identity, revision, digest and evidence row. Both are additive DDL with no domain step or backfill, so repeated apply and verify remain no-op after the first successful run. Backward: an older binary rejects the newer schema before serving it. Archive and deletion lifecycle enforcement is runtime behavior over this state, not a further persisted encoding change. Scope deletion never removes another Scope's rows, and physical erasure is not provided or claimed.
